filename: Sensitivity of Ocean Carbon Sink Estimates to Rare Observations.pdf
title: Sensitivity of Ocean Carbon Sink Estimates to Rare Observations
code_availability: Data analysis scripts and supporting files for the LDEO reconstruction methods are publicly available at https://github.com/OceanCarbon-LDEO-Columbia/ and at https://github.com/OceanCarbon-LDEO-Columbia/pCO2Residual_Testbed for the CMIP6 testbed.
testbed_rationale: The CMIP6 testbed and observational workflows in this study are designed for observing system simulation experiments (OSSEs) and spatiotemporal reconstruction/gap-filling of surface ocean pCO2, rather than for training or evaluating ML parameterizations or climate model emulators.
pain_points: Severe observational data sparsity (SOCAT represents roughly 2% of the global ocean surface) causing high reconstruction sensitivity to small numbers of observations in under-sampled regions like the Southern Ocean.
Decadal and interannual divergence between model ensembles (GOBMs) and observation-based statistical reconstructions.
Declining annual additions of in situ fCO2 measurements to SOCAT since 2017.
Susceptibility of ML reconstructions to observational bias when sparse cruise observations are added.
extraction_notes: The paper uses two ML methods (pCO2-Residual and LDEO-HPD), both utilizing XGBoost, to evaluate the effect of adding SOCATv2024 data (specifically in the Southern Ocean) on air-sea carbon sink estimates and evaluates reconstruction fidelity using a 45-member CMIP6 model testbed.
